title: 1977 AHSME Problem 13
statement: If \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) \(\ldots\) is a sequence of positive numbers such that \(a_{n+2}=a_na_{n+1}\) for all positive integers \(n,\) then the sequence \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) \(\ldots\) is a geometric progression

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: for all positive values of \(a_1\) and \(a_2\)

solutions.text:
The next terms are \(a_3=a_1a_2,\) \(a_4=a_1a_2^2,\) and \(a_5=a_1^2a_2^3.\) If the sequence is geometric, then \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{a_2}{a_1}&=\frac{a_3}{a_2}=a_1,\\ \frac{a_4}{a_3}&=a_2=a_1. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(a_2=a_1^2\) and \(a_2=a_1.\) Positivity forces \(a_1=a_2=1.\) Conversely, these initial values produce the constant geometric sequence \(1,1,1,\ldots.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write out \(a_3,\) \(a_4,\) and \(a_5\) in terms of \(a_1,\) \(a_2\)
Equate the first three successive ratios and use positivity
